description:
Problem: Traditional farming suffers from high water waste, manual labor, and delayed detection of crop health issues due to a lack of real-time soil and environmental data.

Solution: Agri-Rover is an ESP32-CAM powered autonomous robot using ESP-NOW. It integrates computer vision for navigation, environmental sensors, and a target-specific micro-pump that irrigates only dry soil to optimize resource efficiency.
summary: Smallholder farms frequently lose time, water, and yield due to delayed crop disease diagnosis and inefficient manual resource management. To solve this, we developed the Next-Gen AI Agricultural Rover—an autonomous edge-vision mobile platform designed for early disease detection and closed-loop precision agriculture. Operating on an ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 CAM module with 8MB PSRAM, the rover autonomously scans for visual field markers, executes targeted forward drives, and deploys a motorized soil probe. It simultaneously captures high-resolution plant imagery for early leaf disease identification alongside live soil moisture, temperature, and humidity telemetry, streaming everything directly to a real-time mobile Flask web dashboard. By catching plant health issues before they spread and automating targeted irrigation, our low-cost solution prevents crop loss, reduces water waste, and delivers immediate, data-driven insights for sustainable farming.
details:
What does it do & how does it work?

The Next-Gen AI Agricultural Rover is a closed-loop autonomous platform that detects crop health issues early, senses soil conditions locally, and executes precision actions where crops need them most. Powered by an ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 CAM (N16R8) microcontroller with 8MB PSRAM, the rover continuously scans its live camera feed for visual boundary markers. Upon locking onto a target, it executes a controlled forward drive, halts, pans its camera 90° left to capture high-resolution plant imagery for early disease assessment, and lowers a motorized soil probe. It collects real-time soil moisture, ambient temperature, and humidity data, communicates wirelessly via ESP-NOW with a dedicated motor/pump driver node, and logs timestamped plant snapshots and telemetry directly to a mobile Flask web dashboard.

What benefits does it have & what is the intended impact?

  • Early Disease Detection: Captures close-up visual plant imagery and tracks environmental stress factors (humidity/temperature) to identify crop diseases early before infections spread across the field.
  • Resource Efficiency: Target-driven irrigation reduces water waste by up to 30% and prevents chemical fertilizer runoff.
  • Labor Reduction: Automates repetitive row-by-row crop inspection and soil sampling, saving smallholder farmers hours of manual labor.

What tools, hardware, and coding languages were used?

  • Hardware: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 CAM (N16R8) with 8MB PSRAM, ESP32 Driver Node, DHT22 temperature/humidity sensor, analog capacitive soil moisture sensor, SG90/MG90S servos for camera pan and probe deployment, and a 2S 18650 Li-ion battery pack with BMS and buck converter.
  • Software & Languages: C++ (Arduino IDE) for embedded vision and control firmware, Python (Flask) for the local mobile web server and cycle history logging, HTML/CSS/JavaScript for the responsive dashboard UI, and ESP-NOW for low-latency routerless wireless communication.

Creativity & Design Factors

Our design achieves an optimal balance of performance and accessibility by pairing high-stability 8MB PSRAM with onboard edge-vision color tracking. This architecture enables continuous, real-time image processing and wireless telemetry streaming on an ultra-low-cost microcontroller without requiring heavy cloud compute infrastructure. By integrating robust embedded vision with modular hardware, our rover delivers a field-ready, scalable robotics solution that brings enterprise-grade precision agriculture within reach of smallholder farmers and educational innovators.
